presets.name: Warm System
presets.description: The style ships fourteen planet colors evenly spaced around the wheel. This keeps the warm half, so a set of these reads as one system rather than a sample chart.

presets.name: Cool System
presets.description: The other half of the same wheel. Useful next to Warm System when two groups of avatars need to be told apart at a glance.

presets.name: Greyscale
presets.summary: A monochrome sky and a grey planet.
presets.description: Strips the color from a style that is mostly color. What is left is the composition: a disc, a moon and a field of stars.

presets.name: Duotone
presets.summary: One indigo for sky, planet and moon.
presets.description: Three steps of the same hue. The most restrained this style gets, and the easiest to place next to an existing brand color.

presets.name: Muted
presets.summary: Dusty planets against a deep sky.
presets.description: The style's planets are fully saturated. These are not, which turns them from marbles into something more like photographs.

presets.name: Electric
presets.description: The other direction: colors past anything the style ships, on the darkest of its own skies so they read as lit from within.

presets.name: Daylight
presets.summary: A pale sky instead of deep space.
presets.description: The one preset that abandons the night. A light sky turns the planet into a flat disc and the stars vanish into it, which is a different picture rather than a lit version of the same one.

presets.name: Close Up
presets.summary: Scaled in, so the planet fills the frame.
presets.description: Uses scale rather than color. At avatar size the stars turn to noise, and cropping in trades them for a planet you can actually see.
